title: Deducing a rate equation from initial rates
stem: The reaction 2A + B → C was studied at 298 K. The initial rate was measured for three different starting mixtures.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Deduce the order of reaction with respect to A and to B, and write the rate equation.
markscheme: experiments 1 and 2: doubling [A] quadruples rate, so second order in A
experiments 1 and 3: tripling [B] triples rate, so first order in B

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the value of the rate constant, k, and state its units.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate the initial rate when [A] = 0.30 mol dm⁻³ and [B] = 0.20 mol dm⁻³ at 298 K.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A proposed mechanism has a slow first step A + A → A₂ followed by a fast step A₂ + B → C. Explain whether this mechanism is consistent with your rate equation.
markscheme: a slow step involving only two A predicts rate = k[A]² / B appears only after the rate-determining step, so the rate would be zero order in B, but the data show first order in B
parts.notes: Award [1] for a correct prediction of the rate equation from the mechanism even if the conclusion is missing.

title: Making sulfur trioxide
stem:
Sulfur trioxide is made industrially from sulfur dioxide and oxygen in the presence of a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst:
2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g)   ΔH = −196 kJ
In a laboratory model, 0.40 mol of SO₂ and 0.15 mol of O₂ are placed in a sealed vessel.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine the limiting reactant and the maximum amount, in mol, of SO₃ that could form.
markscheme: 0.40 mol SO₂ needs 0.20 mol O₂ but only 0.15 mol is present, so O₂ is limiting

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write the expression for the equilibrium constant, K.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Predict, with reasons, the effect of increasing the temperature on the equilibrium yield of SO₃ and on the value of K.
markscheme: yield of SO₃ decreases / equilibrium shifts left
forward reaction is exothermic so the endothermic (backward) reaction is favoured to absorb the added heat

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Explain, using collision theory, why the rate of reaction increases at higher temperature. Refer to a Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution in your answer.
markscheme: particles have greater average kinetic energy / move faster so collide more frequently
Maxwell–Boltzmann curve shifts to the right / flattens so a greater proportion of particles have E ≥ Ea
so more frequent successful collisions (greater proportion of collisions are successful)
parts.notes: The key mark is the increased proportion of particles with energy ≥ Ea.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: State the effect of the catalyst on the position of equilibrium and on the time taken to reach equilibrium.
markscheme: no effect on the position of equilibrium / yield
equilibrium is reached faster (forward and backward rates increase equally)
